questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

The diagram shows a circle with centre O and radius 40 cm. Points A, B and C lie on the circumference and ∠AOC=1.9 radians; arc ABC is the corresponding arc. [Diagram not to scale.]
(a) Find the length of arc ABC. [2]
(b) Find the perimeter of sector OABC. [2]
(c) Find the area of sector OABC. [2]
questions.summary: Calculate arc length, sector perimeter and sector area.
questions.solution: Arc length rθ=40(1.9)=76 cm. Sector perimeter=76+2(40)=156 cm. Sector area=(1/2)r²θ=(1/2)(1600)(1.9)=1520 cm².

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 7]

The maximum temperature T, in degrees Celsius, in a park on six randomly selected days and the number of visitors N are shown.
[Table: T: 4,5,17,31,29,11; N: 24,26,36,38,46,28.]
The relationship is modelled by N=aT+b.
(a) (i) Find a and b. (ii) Write down r. [4]
(b) Estimate N when T=15°C. [3]
questions.summary: Find and use a linear regression model.
questions.solution: Calculator linear regression gives a=0.667315≈0.667, b=22.2117≈22.2 and r=0.922958≈0.923. At T=15, N=0.667315(15)+22.2117=32.2214, so estimate 32 visitors.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 6]

The diagram shows y=f(x), for −6≤x≤−2. The points (−6,6) and (−2,6) lie on f, with a minimum at (−4,0). [Smooth U-shaped graph.]
(a) Write down the range of f. [2]
Let g(x)=f(x−5). (b) On the grid, sketch g. [2]
(c) Write down the domain of g. [2]
questions.summary: Determine range and translate a function graph.
questions.solution: The range is 0≤y≤6. Since g(x)=f(x−5), translate f five units right: endpoints become (−1,6),(3,6), and minimum (1,0). The domain is −1≤x≤3.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]

The depth of water is d(t)=p cos(qt)+7.5, for 0≤t≤12, where t is hours after high tide. At high tide depth is 9.7 m. At low tide, 7 hours later, depth is 5.3 m.
(a) Find p. [2] (b) Find q. [2] (c) Find d(10). [2]
questions.summary: Determine and use a cosine tidal model.
questions.solution: At t=0, p+7.5=9.7, so p=2.2. High-to-low is half a period, so period=14 and q=2π/14=π/7. Then d(10)=2.2cos(10π/7)+7.5=7.01 m.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider a geometric sequence where the first term is 768 and the second term is 576. Find the least value of n such that the nth term is less than 7.
questions.summary: Solve an exponential inequality for a geometric term.
questions.solution: r=576/768=0.75, so uₙ=768(0.75)^(n−1). Solving 768(0.75)^(n−1)<7 gives n>17.3301. Thus the least integer is n=18 (indeed u₁₇≈7.70 and u₁₈≈5.77).

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 8]

Let f(x)=x²−1 and g(x)=x²−2, for x∈ℝ.
(a) Show that (f∘g)(x)=x⁴−4x²+3. [2]
(b) On the grid, sketch (f∘g)(x), for 0≤x≤2.25. [3]
(c) The equation (f∘g)(x)=k has exactly two solutions, for 0≤x≤2.25. Find the possible values of k. [3]
questions.summary: Compose quadratics and analyze a quartic graph.
questions.solution: f(g(x))=(x²−2)²−1=x⁴−4x²+3. On the interval it starts at (0,3), decreases to minimum (√2,−1), then rises (crossing at x=1 and √3). A horizontal line has exactly two intersections when −1<k≤3; at k=3 one intersection is x=0 and another positive, while k=−1 is tangent and gives only one. Thus k∈(−1,3].

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 6]

Note: distance is in metres and time in seconds. A particle moves along a horizontal line starting at A. Its velocity is v(t)=(2t²−4t)/(t²−2t+2), for 0≤t≤5. The graph is shown, with t-intercepts (0,0) and (2,0). Find the maximum distance from A during 0≤t≤5 and justify.
questions.summary: Compare displacement extrema from a velocity graph.
questions.solution: Distance from A is |s(t)| where s(t)=∫₀ᵗv(u)du. Candidates for maximum occur at t=2 and endpoint t=5. Numerical integration gives s(2)=−2.28318 and s(5)=1.55513. Hence |s(2)|>|s(5)|, so the maximum distance is 2.28 m, attained at t=2.

questions.accessible_text:
8. [Maximum mark: 15]

Let f(x)=−0.5x⁴+3x²+2x. The graph has x-intercepts 0 and p, a maximum A at x=a, and point of inflexion B at x=b.
(a) Find p. [2]
(b) (i) Write down A. (ii) Write down the rate of change at A. [3]
(c) (i) Find B. (ii) Find the rate of change at B. [7]
(d) Region R enclosed by f, the x-axis, x=b and x=a is rotated 360° about the x-axis. Find the volume. [3]
questions.summary: Analyze a quartic and compute a volume of revolution.
questions.solution: Numerically solving f(x)=0 gives the positive root p=2.73205≈2.73. Solving f′=0 gives a=1.87938 and f(a)=8.11721, so A≈(1.88,8.12), with rate 0. Since f″=−6x²+6, the positive inflexion has b=1 and B=(1,4.5); f′(1)=6. The volume is π∫₁^1.87938[f(x)]²dx=128.890≈129.

questions.accessible_text:
9. [Maximum mark: 15]

A ship sails north A→D. C is 175 km north of A and D is 60 km north of C. Island E has bearing 055° from A and 134° from C. [Diagram not to scale.]
(a) Find bearing of A from E. [2] (b) Find CE. [5] (c) Find DE. [3]
(d) At D the ship travels directly to E at 50 km/h. Simultaneously a boat starts from B on AC, where B is closest to E. They arrive together. Find boat speed. [5]
questions.summary: Use bearings, sine/cosine rules and equal travel times.
questions.solution: The reverse bearing is 055°+180°=235°. Triangle ACE has angles A=55°, C=46° (since CA bearing 180° and CE 134°), E=79°. By sine rule CE/sin55°=175/sin79°, giving CE=146 km. In triangle CDE, included angle DCE=134°, so DE²=60²+CE²−2(60)(CE)cos134°, giving DE=193 km. Since BE⊥AC, BE=CE sin46°=105 km. Equal times give DE/50=BE/v, so v=50BE/DE=27.3 km/h.

questions.accessible_text:
10. [Maximum mark: 15]

A probability distribution has x: 0,1,2,3 and P(X=x): p, 1/2, 3/10, q, where E(X)=1.2.
(a) (i) Find q. (ii) Find p. [4]
A bag has at least three white and three blue marbles. Three are drawn without replacement; X is the number of blue marbles.
(b) (i) Write down P(three blue). (ii) Explain why P(three white)=1/6. (iii) The bag has ten marbles, w white. Find w. [5]
A game wins if three white are drawn. (c) Jill plays nine times. Find P(exactly two prizes). [2]
(d) Grant plays until two prizes. Find P(second prize on eighth attempt). [4]
questions.summary: Determine a distribution and apply binomial/negative-binomial probabilities.
questions.solution: E(X)=1/2+2(3/10)+3q=1.2 gives q=1/30. Summing probabilities gives p=1−1/2−3/10−1/30=1/6. Thus P(three blue)=1/30 and P(three white)=P(X=0)=1/6. With ten marbles, C(w,3)/C(10,3)=1/6, so w=6. Jill: C(9,2)(1/6)²(5/6)⁷=0.279. Grant needs exactly one win in first seven and a win on attempt 8: C(7,1)(1/6)(5/6)⁶(1/6)=0.0651.
